description:
Trigger: client sends { "filter": { "unknownField": "x" } } or { "filter": { "foo": 1, "relatedIds": ["EM1"] } }. MetadataFilterCondition has all-Option fields and no deny_unknown_fields, so the second value deserializes to Default::default(). The cross-field validate_metadata_filter() (metadata.rs:553-565) sees a Condition with related_ids=None, related_type=None and returns Ok(()) — passing validation. The generic handle_query then re-parses the same filter, which also succeeds, and queries with an empty filter — returning ALL objects.

Actual bad behavior: when a client sends a deliberately mistyped filter clause (typo, vendor extension, future spec field), the server silently returns all objects instead of either: (a) honoring the relatedIds + relatedType constraint check, or (b) returning unsupportedFilter. The §3.4.1 invariant the validator was added to enforce can be bypassed by also misspelling another field — relatedIds will deserialize but be silently dropped in the round-trip because field name 'relatedIds' is camelCase-correct, but a typo'd 'related_ids' would be eaten as 'unknown field'.

Specifically dangerous: { "filter": { "related_ids": ["EM1"] } } (Rust-style snake_case) deserializes to MetadataFilterCondition::default() (all None) — no constraint violation detected. Client thinks it filtered; server returns all.

Probe (do not run): assert that handle_metadata_query rejects { "filter": { "related_ids": ["EM1"] } } with either unsupportedFilter or invalidArguments. Currently it will succeed and return all objects.
title: Filter dispatch validation skipped when malformed filter deserializes successfully as default MetadataFilterCondition
